POVM, projectivity, and Cauchy--Schwarz suffice for the counterexample and
the proposed source proof. The counterexample below is a mathematical
calculation, not a kernel-certified Lean instance.

\section{Key theorem forms}

Let $\widehat\psi$ be the normalized expanded state of a projective strategy
winning the Pauli basis test with probability at least $1-\eps$. Write
$L^W_f(\ell)$ and $M^W_a(u)$ for its expanded line and point effects. For
the subline law $D$, abbreviate the two correlations by
\begin{align*}
 A(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z)M^X_{f_X(x)}(x))\widehat\psi\rangle,\\
 B(T)&=\E_D\E_{(x,z,\alpha,\beta)\in\ell}
   \sum_{f_X,f_Z}\langle\widehat\psi,
   (T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\ot
     M^Z_{f_Z(z)}(z))\widehat\psi\rangle.
\end{align*}
The paper's Claim 17-2 states
\[
 |A(T)-B(T)|\leq O\bigl(m\sqrt{\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)}\bigr)
 \quad\text{for}\quad
 T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The former Lean declaration quantified instead over every paired-line POVM
with the degree support and evaluated consistency conclusions of the
combined-lines lemma. Its scalar errors $\delta_P,\delta_Q$ were arbitrary,
independently of $\eps$. The right-hand side remained the same, with
$\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}(\eps)=\sqrt\eps$.

\section{The construction used by the source}

The paired-line measurement is defined by the displayed sandwich in the
proof of the combined-lines lemma. Claim 17-2 uses this definition to sum
over the Z polynomial:
\[
 \sum_{f_Z}T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
   \Bigl(\sum_{f_Z}L^Z_{f_Z}(\ell_Z)\Bigr)L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X)
 =L^X_{f_X}(\ell_X).
\]
The last equality uses completeness and projectivity. Cauchy--Schwarz
reduces the scalar difference to the square root of the resulting
X-line/point consistency deficit. The separate X marginal of the subline
law is sufficient; no joint conditional law for $(x,z)$ is needed.
Restriction to a line kind and coordinate costs a factor $2m$, so the
resulting square-root estimate is bounded by the paper's stated error
because $m\geq1$.\footnote{The construction is at lines 942--949 and the
claim and calculation at lines 1168--1201 of
\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex},
labels \path{lem:qld-xz-lines} and \path{claim:17-2} in
\cite{Ji2020MIPStar}. The repair is tracked by \ghissue{414}; the earlier
proof attempt is \ghissue{405}.}

\section{A counterexample to the enlarged domain}

Choose an admissible tuple with $q>1$ and a perfect projective strategy.
The honest strategy in the completeness lemma supplies one; for example,
$(q,m,d)=(8,1,1)$ is admissible. Its expanded state has norm one. For
$a\in\F_q$, let $c_a$ be the constant polynomial with value $a$. For both
players and every line pair, define a POVM by
\[
 T_{c_a,c_b}=q^{-2}I\quad(a,b\in\F_q),\qquad
 T_{f_X,f_Z}=0\quad\text{for every other pair}.
\]
There are $q^2$ nonzero effects, so they sum to $I$. Both axis-degree
requirements hold. At any incident point a constant polynomial has a
uniquely determined value, even on a zero-direction line. Thus the optional
evaluation in Lean returns the ordinary field value, never an undefined
outcome, for every nonzero effect in this example.

The evaluated POVM is uniform on the $q^2$ point pairs. Against any complete
joint point measurement $Q$, its agreement is $q^{-2}$ and its consistency
defect is $1-q^{-2}$. Therefore the line-witness requirements hold with
$\delta_P=1$ in every opposite placement. A point witness also exists within
the former public domain: take the projective measurement which always
answers $(0,0)$. It is exactly self-consistent and has both ordered-product
distances at most $4$. Indeed, the squared norms of either ordered product
family sum to one, by projectivity and completeness, and
\begin{align*}
 \sum_{a,b}\|(Q_{a,b}-M^X_aM^Z_b)\widehat\psi\|^2
 &\leq 2\sum_{a,b}\|Q_{a,b}\widehat\psi\|^2\\
 &\quad+2\sum_{a,b}\|M^X_aM^Z_b\widehat\psi\|^2\\
 &=4.
\end{align*}
The reversed ordering satisfies the same calculation. Hence $\delta_Q=4$
is allowed by every point-witness field. These constants are permitted by
the former scalar quantifiers; the argument does not require them to be
polynomially small functions of $\eps$.

For each supported subline sample, completeness gives
\[
 A(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
    (I\ot M^Z_bM^X_a)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-2},
 \qquad
 B(T)=q^{-2}\sum_{a,b}\langle\widehat\psi,
    (I\ot M^Z_b)\widehat\psi\rangle=q^{-1}.
\]
The first equality uses $\sum_bM^Z_b\sum_aM^X_a=I$, without a commutation
assumption. Probability averaging preserves these constants. The absolute
difference is therefore $(q-1)/q^2>0$, whereas the claimed bound is zero at
$\eps=0$. For $q=8$ the difference is $7/64$. The same perfect strategy is
admissible at arbitrarily small positive $\eps$, so excluding zero or
enlarging a universal constant cannot repair the claim. No polynomially
vanishing error depending on $\eps$ alone absorbs this difference.

\begin{lemma}[Combined point measurements]
	\label{lem:qld-4-10}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.CombinedPointsWitness}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_combinedPointsWitness}
	\leanok
	\uses{def:expanded-state, def:expanded-point-measurement,
		def:povm-distance, def:symmetric-equivalents}
	There exists a function $\delta_Q(\eps) = \poly(\eps)$ such that the
	following holds. For every $x, z \in \F_q^m$ and
	$\hilb \in \{\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}, \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}\}$ there are
	projective measurements $\{\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\}_{a,b \in \F_q}$ acting
	on $\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$ such that:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item (\textbf{Self-consistency}) On average over uniformly random
		$x, z \in \F_q^m$,
		\begin{equation}
			\label{eq:qld-q-self-cons}
			(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
			\approx_{\delta_Q}
			(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,.
		\end{equation}
		\item (\textbf{Consistency with $\hat{M}$}) On average over uniformly
		random $x, z \in \F_q^m$,
		\begin{gather}
			\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz}
			(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
			\approx_{\delta_Q}
			(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a} \,
			\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,
			\\
			\label{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx}
			(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
			\approx_{\delta_Q}
			(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b} \,
			\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,.
		\end{gather}
	\end{enumerate}
	Furthermore, all symmetric equivalents of these approximations also hold.
	The operators $\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a}$ and
	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b}$ do not commute in general, so the
	products in \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-xz} and
	\eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} differ and the two relations are separate
	conclusions.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\leanok
	\uses{lem:qld-comm-cons, lem:ortho, fact:triangle,
		def:expanded-point-measurement, def:symmetric-equivalents,
		def:povm-distance}
	The formal proof works with field-valued outcomes directly. On each
	expanded local space form the complete sandwich POVM
	$R^{x,z}_{a,b}=M^{Z,z}_b M^{X,x}_a M^{Z,z}_b$.
	Field-valued approximate commutation bounds its distance from the ordered
	point product. Point self-consistency and the same commutation estimate
	bound its off-diagonal overlap across opposite placements.
	Apply orthonormalization to obtain a projective measurement for each
	point pair, on the same expanded local space, close to this POVM.
	The squared-distance triangle inequality gives self-consistency of the
	projective families and their distances from both ordered products.
	The placement comparisons give all symmetric equivalents.
	The estimates are absorbed into $\delta_Q(\eps)=K\eps^{1/8}$ for one
	universal constant $K$.

	This proves the stated measurement construction without using the source's
	intermediate binary refinements and quantum linearity construction.
	The zero-state padding needed by that source proof remains the separate
	import issue in Remark~\ref{rem:linearity-import} and
	\cite{gap:qpbt_linearity-theorem-quotation}.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Formalization support for coefficient polynomial agreement]
	\label{lem:coefficient-polynomial-agreement}

	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_eq_ofFn,

		MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_injective,
		MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePolynomialOfCoefficients_natDegree_le}
	\leanok
	Let $K$ be a finite integral domain, let $c\in\N$, and let
	$f,g\in K^{c+1}$ be distinct coefficient vectors. Their polynomials
	$p_f(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}f_iT^i$ and $p_g(T)=\sum_{i=0}^{c}g_iT^i$
	agree at at most $c$ elements of $K$.
	The coefficient representation is injective, preserves evaluation,
	and has natural degree at most $c$.
	This is a formalization-only auxiliary for the Schwartz--Zippel step
	in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}
	(\texttt{14\_analysis\_of\_the\_pauli\_basis\_test.tex:955}).
	There is no restriction $c<|K|$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\leanok
	The coefficient representation is injective, preserves evaluation,
	and gives polynomials of degree at most $c$. If the polynomials agreed
	at more than $c$ elements, the univariate root bound applied to their
	difference would force them to be equal, contradicting $f\ne g$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[Combined line measurements]
	\label{lem:qld-xz-lines}

	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.exists_combinedLinesWitness}

	two-variable polynomial error read in the corrected sum sense of
	\cite{gap:qpbt_pasting-product-error}, that is, a bound
	$C\bigl(\eps^{r} + (md/q)^{s}\bigr)$ with $C \ge 1$ and $r, s > 0$ on the
	closed nonnegative quadrant rather than the literal product form of the
	shorthand, such that the following holds. For
	$\hilb \in \{\hilb_{\mathsf{A}}, \hilb_{\mathsf{B}}\}$ and every pair of
	lines $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ in $\F_q^m$ there exists a POVM
	$\{T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\}$ acting on $\hilb \ot (\C^q)^{\ot M}$,
	with answers consisting of pairs of polynomials
	$(f_X, f_Z) \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X) \times \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, such that on
	average over pairs $(\ell_X, x)$ and $(\ell_Z, z)$ independently sampled
	from the line-point distribution
	(Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}),
	\[
		\big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}
		_{[\mathrm{eval}_x(\cdot)=a,\ \mathrm{eval}_z(\cdot)=b]}
		\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
		\simeq_{\delta_P}
		\big(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}\,,
	\]
	as well as all symmetric equivalents of this approximation. Moreover, if
	$\ell_W$ is axis-parallel, then $f_W \in \deg_{d}(\ell_W)$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\uses{def:expanded-line-measurement, lem:qld-4-10, fact:add-a-proj,
		lem:cool-closeness-fact, lem:qld-comm-line-cons, fact:agreement,
		fact:data-processing, lem:pasting, lem:schwartz-zippel-total-degree,
		def:symmetric-equivalents, def:concrete-paired-line-measurement,
		lem:concrete-paired-line-degree-support}
	Define, for all lines $\ell_X, \ell_Z$ and
	$(f_X, f_Z) \in \deg_{md}(\ell_X) \times \deg_{md}(\ell_Z)$, the sandwich
	operator
	$T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
	= \hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},Z),\ell_Z}_{f_Z}
	\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}$,
	which forms a valid POVM; since the lines measurements come from a valid
	strategy for the low-degree test, on an axis-parallel line $\ell_W$ the
	outcome $f_W$ lies in $\deg_d(\ell_W)$, and this property is inherited by
	$T$. As intermediate consistency relations, write
	$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet} = \sum_b \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ and
	$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{\bullet,b} = \sum_a \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ for the two
	marginals of the combined point measurement of
	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-10}. Applying
	Lemma~\ref{fact:add-a-proj} to \eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} and then
	Lemma~\ref{lem:cool-closeness-fact} gives, on average over uniform
	$x, z$,
	$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
	\approx_\delta
	\sum_b (\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
	(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$,
	and a direct norm computation from this display and
	\eqref{eq:qld-q-cons-m-hat-zx} yields the marginal consistencies
	$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_{\delta_Q}
	(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},X),x}_{a})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$ and
	$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{\bullet,b})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \approx_{\delta_Q}
	(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Point},Z),z}_{b})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$.

	between $\approx$ and $\simeq$ with Lemma~\ref{fact:agreement} and
	summing outcomes with Lemma~\ref{fact:data-processing}, the lines
	measurements are consistent with the points measurements, and combining
	with the marginal consistencies gives, on average over the line-point
	distribution,
	$(\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,\bullet})_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'} \simeq_{\delta_Q}
	(\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}
	_{[\mathrm{eval}_x(\cdot)=a]})_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}$

	from the pasting lemma (Lemma~\ref{lem:pasting}) applied with
	$\hat{Q}^{x,z}_{a,b}$ in the role of the combined measurement,
	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}$ and
	$\hat{M}^{(\mathrm{Line},Z),\ell_Z}$ in the roles of the two factor
	measurements, $T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}$ in the role of the pasted measurement,

\end{proof}

\begin{definition}[The concrete paired-line POVM]
	\label{def:concrete-paired-line-measurement}

		def:ideg-deg-polynomials}
	For any projective setting, either player, and any two source lines,
	define the POVM on the expanded local space by
	\[
		T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}
		=\hat M^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X}
		 \hat M^{(\mathrm{Line},Z),\ell_Z}_{f_Z}
		 \hat M^{(\mathrm{Line},X),\ell_X}_{f_X},
		\qquad (f_X,f_Z)\in\deg_{md}(\ell_X)\times\deg_{md}(\ell_Z).

	gives the identity by completeness and projectivity of the line
	measurements. This is the construction in the proof of
	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines} in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar}.
\end{definition}

\begin{lemma}[Restricted line distributions and error inflation]
	\label{lem:restricted-line-mixture-bounds}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.linePointDist_eq_mixture_restricted}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.avg_restricted_le, MIPStarRE.QPBT.avg_restricted_prod_le}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.restricted_lines_consistency_bound}
	\leanok
	% Source: unlabelled prose in the paper --- the discussion following
	% def:ith-restricted-line at lines 1049-1061 of
	% references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex.
	\uses{def:ith-restricted-line, def:line-point-dist, lem:qld-xz-lines,
		lem:qld-4-10, def:expanded-state}
	The distribution $D_{\mathrm{ALine}}$ is a uniform mixture of the
	distributions $D_{\mathrm{ALine},i}$ for $i \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$, and
	likewise $D_{\mathrm{DLine}}$ is a uniform mixture of the
	$D_{\mathrm{DLine},i}$. As a consequence:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item any approximation that holds on average over the line-point
		distribution $D_{\mathrm{Line}}$ with error $\delta$ holds over each
		restricted distribution $D_{\mathrm{ALine},i}$ and
		$D_{\mathrm{DLine},i}$ with error $2m\delta$;
		\item any approximation that holds on average over
		$D_{\mathrm{Line}} \times D_{\mathrm{Line}}$ holds over any product
		of restricted distributions with error $4m^2\delta$;
		\item in particular, by Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}, for any types
		$\mathrm{v}_1, \mathrm{v}_2 \in \{\mathrm{ALine},
		\mathrm{DLine}\}$ and any $i, j \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$,
		\begin{equation}
			\label{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}
			\E_{(\ell_X,x) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_1,i}}\
			\E_{(\ell_Z,z) \sim D_{\mathrm{v}_2,j}}
			\sum_{f_X,f_Z}
			\bra{\hat\psi}
			\big(T^{\ell_X,\ell_Z}_{f_X,f_Z}\big)_{\mathsf{A}\mathsf{A}'}
			\ot
			\big(\Id - \hat{Q}^{x,z}_{f_X(x),f_Z(z)}
			\big)_{\mathsf{B}\mathsf{A}''}
			\ket{\hat\psi}
			= O(m^2 \delta_P)\,.
		\end{equation}
	\end{enumerate}
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\leanok
	\uses{lem:qld-xz-lines, def:line-point-dist, def:consistency}
	The line-point distribution places weight $\tfrac{1}{2}$ on each of the
	axis-parallel and diagonal components and, within each component, uniform
	weight on the index $i$, so each restricted distribution carries mixture
	weight $\tfrac{1}{2m}$ in $D_{\mathrm{Line}}$. A nonnegative average that
	is at most $\delta$ therefore bounds each mixture component by
	$2m\delta$, and products of two such mixtures give the factor
	$(2m)^2 = 4m^2$. The instance \eqref{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted} is item
	2 applied to the conclusion of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-xz-lines}, whose
	$\simeq_{\delta_P}$ relation over two independent copies of the
	line-point distribution is precisely the statement that the left-hand
	side of \eqref{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}, averaged over
	$D_{\mathrm{Line}} \times D_{\mathrm{Line}}$, is at most $\delta_P$.
\end{proof}

\begin{lemma}[The sub-line distribution]
	\label{lem:qld-sublines}
	\lean{MIPStarRE.QPBT.SubLineWitness}
	\notready
	\uses{def:line, def:line-point-dist, def:ith-restricted-line}
	% Statement as in the source (references/qpbt-paper/
	% 14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, lem:qld-sublines). The
	% line-point distribution over F_q^{2m+2} is built from the index
	% function chi of def:ld-question-distribution at dimension 2m+2, which
	% is defined only when 2m+2 divides q; the source instantiates it
	% without securing this condition. See rem:qld-4-7-divisibility.
	There exists a distribution $D$
	over tuples $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, where $\ell$ is a line in
	$\F_q^{2m+2}$ and $\ell_X, \ell_Z$ are lines in $\F_q^m$, with the
	following properties:
	\begin{enumerate}
		\item The marginal distribution over $\ell$ is the same as the
		marginal of the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$.
		% The source phrases the next property as: the marginal over
		% (ell_X, ell_Z) is "a mixture of the product distributions
		% D_{ALine,i} x D_{ALine,j} and D_{DLine,i} x D_{DLine,j}". Those
		% products are distributions over pairs of line-point pairs, not
		% over pairs of lines, so the phrase does not define the asserted
		% marginal distribution on pairs of lines as written; the
		% formulation below states the mixture at the level of the joint
		% law of (ell_X, ell_Z, u), which is what the proofs of
		% lem:claim-17-2 and lem:claim-17-3 use.
		\item For any point of the form $u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$
		lying on $\ell$, it holds that $u_X \in \ell_X$ and
		$u_Z \in \ell_Z$. Moreover, the joint distribution of
		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z, u)$, for $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z) \sim D$ and
		$u$ chosen uniformly at random on $\ell$, is a mixture of
		components indexed by a type
		$\mathrm{v} \in \{\mathrm{ALine}, \mathrm{DLine}\}$ and indices
		$i, j \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ with the following two properties
		within the component $(\mathrm{v}, i, j)$: the pair
		$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is distributed according to the product of the
		marginal distributions on lines of $D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and of
		$D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the
		point $u_X$ is uniformly distributed on $\ell_X$ and likewise the
		point $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed on $\ell_Z$. Equivalently,
		since under each restricted distribution the point is uniformly
		distributed on the line conditionally on the line: within the
		component $(\mathrm{v}, i, j)$, the pair
		$((\ell_X, u_X), (\ell_Z, z'))$, where $z'$ is a uniformly random
		point of $\ell_Z$ sampled independently of $u$, is distributed
		according to $D_{\mathrm{v},i} \times D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and
		symmetrically the pair $((\ell_X, x'), (\ell_Z, u_Z))$, with $x'$
		a uniformly random point of $\ell_X$ sampled independently of
		$u$, is distributed according to
		$D_{\mathrm{v},i} \times D_{\mathrm{v},j}$. (No assertion is made
		about the joint conditional law of the pair $(u_X, u_Z)$.)
		\item If $\ell$ is axis-parallel, then $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ are
		axis-parallel.
	\end{enumerate}
	(Property~3 is not part of the numbered statement in the source; see
	Remark~\ref{rem:qld-sublines-property-three}.)
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
	\uses{def:line-representative, def:ld-question-distribution,
		def:line-point-dist, def:ith-restricted-line, def:line,
		prop:line-equiv}
	The distribution $D$ is described by a sampling procedure. First sample
	$(\ell, u)$ from the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and write
	$u = (u_X, u_Z, \alpha, \beta)$, so that Property~1 holds by
	construction; all auxiliary randomness introduced below is sampled
	independently of $(\ell, u)$. As in
	Definition~\ref{def:ith-restricted-line}, write $\bar\chi$ for the
	zero-based shift of the index function at dimension $m$. Its classes
	$\bar\chi^{-1}(i)$ for $i \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ partition $\F_q$
	into sets of equal size $q/m$. Write $\bar\chi_{2m+2}$ for the analogous
	zero-based shift at dimension $2m+2$. For the extended-coordinate index in
	the construction below, write $k=r-1$ when the paper writes $r$; the
	source-line indices $i_X,i_Z$ are shifted in the same way. The function
	$\bar\chi_{2m+2}$ is defined only when $2m+2$ divides $q$, and hence so is
	the line-point distribution over $\F_q^{2m+2}$ from which $(\ell, u)$ is
	drawn
	(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution}); admissibility of
	$(q,m,d)$ supplies only that $m$ divides $q$, and for admissible
	parameters with $m \ge 2$ the required divisibility fails, so this
	first step is an unresolved obligation of the source argument, recorded
	in Remark~\ref{rem:qld-4-7-divisibility} and analyzed in
	\cite{gap:qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility}; the construction below is
	carried out for the parameters for which the distribution is defined.
	By a
	\emph{fresh diagonal direction pair} we mean a pair $(s', w')$ with
	$s'$ uniformly random in $\F_q$ and $w' \in \F_q^m$ having coordinates
	$0, \dots, \bar\chi(s')-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates
	uniformly random; this is exactly the law of the coordinate--direction
	data of the diagonal component of the line-point distribution over
	$\F_q^m$ (Definition~\ref{def:line-point-dist}).

	If $\ell$ is axis-parallel, $\ell = (v, e_k)$ with
	$v = (v_X, v_Z, \alpha_0, \beta_0)$ and $k \in \{0, \dots, 2m+1\}$, set
	$\ell_X = (v'_X, e_{i_X})$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, e_{i_Z})$ where: for
	$0 \le k < m$, $i_X = k$ and $i_Z$ is uniformly random in
	$\{0,\dots,m-1\}$; for $m \le k < 2m$, $i_X$ is uniformly random and
	$i_Z = k - m$; for $2m \le k < 2m+2$, both $i_X$ and $i_Z$ are
	uniformly random; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are the canonical line
	representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the chosen directions
	(Definition~\ref{def:line-representative}), so that $v_X \in \ell_X$
	and $v_Z \in \ell_Z$.

	If $\ell$ is diagonal, $\ell = (v, s, w)$, then by the construction of
	the diagonal component of the line-point distribution
	(Definition~\ref{def:ld-question-distribution} instantiated at
	dimension $2m+2$) the direction $w = (w_X, w_Z, \gamma, \delta)$ has
	coordinates $0, \dots, k-1$ equal to $0$, where
	$k = \bar\chi_{2m+2}(s)$,
	and its remaining coordinates are uniformly random. These remaining
	coordinates may also vanish, so $w$ need not have a nonzero coordinate
	at index $k$ and may be the zero vector, in which case $\ell$ is a
	singleton (Definition~\ref{def:line}).
	% In its one-based notation, the source proof describes w as "a direction
	% vector whose first nonzero coordinate is j = chi(s)"
	% (references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex, proof
	% of lem:qld-sublines); the distribution delivers only the weaker
	% property recorded here, which is the one the argument uses. The
	% source also leaves the laws of s_X and s_Z unspecified ("chosen such
	% that chi(s_X) = j" in its one-based notation); the uniform choices
	% below are needed for the exact marginals claimed in Property 2.
	Sample $\ell_X = (v'_X, s_X, w'_X)$ and $\ell_Z = (v'_Z, s_Z, w'_Z)$
	where: for $0 \le k < m$, $w'_X = w_X$ and $w'_Z = w_Z$, with $s_X$
	uniformly random in the class $\bar\chi^{-1}(k)$ and $s_Z$ uniformly
	random in the class $\bar\chi^{-1}(0)$; for $m \le k < 2m$, the pair
	$(s_X, w'_X)$ is a fresh diagonal direction pair and $w'_Z = w_Z$,
	with $s_Z$ uniformly random in the class $\bar\chi^{-1}(k-m)$; for
	$2m \le k < 2m+2$, both $(s_X, w'_X)$ and $(s_Z, w'_Z)$ are fresh
	diagonal direction pairs, sampled independently; and $v'_X, v'_Z$ are
	the canonical representatives of $v_X, v_Z$ for the directions
	$w'_X, w'_Z$.

	Property~3 is immediate from the procedure: when $\ell$ is
	axis-parallel, both $\ell_X$ and $\ell_Z$ are constructed to be
	axis-parallel. The containments in Property~2 hold for every point
	$u^\dagger = (u^\dagger_X, u^\dagger_Z, \alpha^\dagger,
	\beta^\dagger)$ of $\ell$: the block $u^\dagger_X$ differs from $v_X$
	by a multiple of the direction of $\ell_X$ when that direction is
	inherited from $\ell$ (namely $e_k$ for axis-parallel $\ell$ with
	$0 \le k < m$, and $w_X$ for diagonal $\ell$ with $0 \le k < m$),
	and equals $v_X$ in all other cases, since then the corresponding
	block of the direction of $\ell$ vanishes; in either case
	$u^\dagger_X \in \ell_X$ because $v_X \in \ell_X$, and symmetrically
	$u^\dagger_Z \in \ell_Z$.

	For the distributional part of Property~2, observe first that
	$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is a function of $\ell$ and of the auxiliary
	randomness alone: the directions used are either read off from the
	direction data of $\ell$ or freshly sampled, and by
	Proposition~\ref{prop:line-equiv} the canonical representatives
	$v'_X, v'_Z$ do not depend on which base point of $\ell$ is used to
	compute them. Under both components of the line-point distribution the
	point $u$ is uniformly distributed on $\F_q^{2m+2}$ and, conditioned
	on the line $\ell$, uniformly distributed on the points of $\ell$
	(each of the $q$ values of the line parameter, or the single point
	when the direction vanishes, being equally likely). Hence, conditioned
	on $(\ell, \ell_X, \ell_Z)$, the sampled point $u$ is uniformly
	distributed on $\ell$, and it suffices to establish the claimed
	mixture description for the tuple $(\ell_X, \ell_Z, u)$ produced by
	the procedure itself.

	Condition on the component of the line-point distribution
	(axis-parallel or diagonal) and on $k$; the mixture of Property~2 is
	over these choices together with the fresh index choices, and the
	blocks $u_X, u_Z$ of $u$ are independent and uniform on $\F_q^m$,
	independent of all direction data. In the axis-parallel case with
	$0 \le k < m$, the pair $(\ell_X, u_X)$ consists of the uniformly
	random point $u_X$ together with the canonical axis-parallel line
	through it in direction $e_k$, so
	$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},k}$, while, conditioned
	additionally on $i_Z$, the pair $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ consists of the
	uniformly random point $u_Z$ together with the canonical line through
	it in direction $e_{i_Z}$, so
	$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{ALine},i_Z}$; the two pairs are
	functions of the disjoint independent data $u_X$ and $(u_Z, i_Z)$,
	hence independent. In the diagonal case with $0 \le k < m$, the
	triple $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ has $u_X$ uniform, $w_X$ with coordinates
	$0, \dots, k-1$ equal to $0$ and the remaining coordinates uniform,
	and $s_X$ uniform in $\bar\chi^{-1}(k)$, which is exactly the law
	generating $D_{\mathrm{DLine},k}$; hence
	$(\ell_X, u_X) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},k}$, and similarly
	$(\ell_Z, u_Z) \sim D_{\mathrm{DLine},0}$ since $w_Z$ is uniform and
	$s_Z$ is uniform in $\bar\chi^{-1}(0)$; the two pairs are functions of
	the disjoint independent data $(u_X, w_X, s_X)$ and $(u_Z, w_Z, s_Z)$,
	hence independent. The remaining cases are analogous: each of
	$(\ell_X, u_X)$ and $(\ell_Z, u_Z)$ is either built from the inherited
	direction block as above, or from a fresh axis index or fresh diagonal
	direction pair, in which case it is distributed as the uniform mixture
	over $i \in \{0, \dots, m-1\}$ of $D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ for the
	corresponding type $\mathrm{v}$; and the two pairs are always functions of
	disjoint independent collections of the variables $u_X$, $u_Z$, the
	direction blocks, and the fresh auxiliary choices, hence independent
	conditioned on the component. Within each component this yields exactly the
	description of Property~2: the pair $(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$ is
	product-distributed according to the line marginals of
	$D_{\mathrm{v},i}$ and $D_{\mathrm{v},j}$, and, conditioned on
	$(\ell_X, \ell_Z)$, each of $u_X$ and $u_Z$ is uniformly distributed
	on its line, because under each restricted distribution the point is
	uniform on the line conditionally on the line. The equivalent product
	formulations follow from the same conditional uniformity.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[The error term in the source proof of
	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13}]
	\label{rem:qld-4-13-source-defects}
	The statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-13} retains the source error
	form $\delta_{\mathrm{combine}} = \poly(m^2\eps, md/q)$, which
	remains unproved. The source proof in \cite{Ji2020MIPStar} asserts
	two different bounds for the quantity
	\eqref{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency}: the bound
	$O(m(\eps^{1/4} + \delta_P^{1/4} + \delta_Q^{1/4} +
	\delta_{\mathrm{Line}}^{1/2}))$, obtained by chaining the three
	claims (Lemmas~\ref{lem:claim-17-1}--\ref{lem:claim-17-3}), and the
	bound $O(m^2 \delta_P)$, whose derivation decomposes
	\eqref{eq:qld-combined-lines-consistency} into
	restricted-distribution terms bounded by
	\eqref{eq:qld-xz-lines-restricted}. The second derivation requires a
	joint product law for the pair $((\ell_X, x), (\ell_Z, z))$ that
	Property~2 of Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-sublines} does not provide, and
	neither bound is dominated by a function of $m^2\eps$ and $md/q$
	alone that vanishes as its arguments vanish. The proof above
	therefore follows the first route only and establishes the bound
	$m \cdot \poly(\eps, md/q)$, which is the form consumed by
	Lemma~\ref{lem:qld-4-7}, whose error function absorbs the prefactor
	$m$ into $(md)^a$. The full analysis --- the two routes, the scalings
	showing that the claimed form follows from neither, the corrected
	deficit assertion in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:claim-17-2}, and the
	candidate repairs with their open obligations --- is given in
	\cite{gap:qpbt_combined-lines-error-term}.
\end{remark}

  2030		along such a line either $(\alpha,\beta)$ is constant, in which case

  2032		polynomials of degree at most $d$, or $(x,z)$ is constant, in which case
  2033		$f$ is affine in the line parameter, so in either case

  2035		\ref{lem:claim-17-2} and~\ref{lem:claim-17-3} with the triangle

  2112		projective setting with error $\eps$ be given, together with complete
  2113		projective joint point measurements $Q^{x,z}_{a,b}$ on both expanded local
  2114		spaces. Suppose that, for every directed opposite placement, these
  2115		measurements are self-consistent with squared-distance error at most

+# Issue 512: Recovery of the established extended-line construction
+
+The proof of `exists_extendedLinesWitness_established` was recovered from
+commit `6e8d67ef8ba22de69a0c166adcdf23ba6e7a33aa`, retained at
+`0f4ef05370350f4017439ebd839ef0561f13130f`, onto the isolated issue-512
+worktree based at `ae124f8f09ee002444ac5b9711822c0f1daae142`.
+The preceding receipt is `prover-512-20260912-01.last.md` in the local
+session archive. This is recovery of that proof, not a new mathematical attempt.
+
+This audit is the reader-facing record of that provenance. The Lean module and
+theorem docstrings carry only mathematical source and gap references; the
+commit-level recovery history of each module is kept here instead.
+
+## Scope
+
+The recovered declarations and the modules holding them:
+
+- `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Lines/{Sampling,PointComparison,Conditioning,
+  Construction}.lean`
+- `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/{XEvalDeficit,SubLineXDeficit}.lean`
+- `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/ExtendedLines/{Measurement,Overlap,Estimates}.lean`
+- the target `exists_extendedLinesWitness_established` in
+  `MIPStarRE/QPBT/Combining/Apply.lean`
+
+Each of these modules was recovered from the saved commit named above. The
+blueprint counterpart is the formalization-support node
+`lem:qld-4-13-established` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex`;
+the paired-line consistency theorem it rests on is recorded in
+`lem:combined-line-measurement-consistency` and the supporting nodes beside it.
+
+## Source of Truth
+
+The source is `references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex`,
+`lem:qld-xz-lines` (882-961), `lem:qld-4-10` (689-709), and
+`lem:qld-4-13` with its first proof route (1020-1034, 1118-1246).
+The auxiliary blueprint entry is `lem:qld-4-13-established`. The divergences
+between that entry and the printed lemma are governed by
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_combined-lines-error-term.tex` and
+`docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_ld-dimension-divisibility.tex`.
+
+## Findings
+
+### Construction and provenance
+
+Only declarations needed by the construction were recovered. Existing proofs
+of the combined point witness, subline law, Z deficits, polynomial absorption,
+projection contraction, and heterogeneous pasting were reused. No file from
+another worktree was changed, and the saved branch was neither merged nor copied
+wholesale. The recovered material is divided into modules below 1000 lines.
+
+- `Lines/Sampling`, `PointComparison`, `Conditioning`, and `Construction`
+  recover the needed declarations from saved `Combining/Lines.lean`. The
+  X-Z-X measurement is unchanged. Conditioning is on nonzero X directions;
+  its mass is at least one half, and the discarded contribution is restored
+  with the bound `1/(2q)` under the original product law.
+- The current `combined_line_measurement_consistency` statement is unchanged
+  and moved to `Lines/Construction`. The existing witness constructors now
+  use its proved value. The current heterogeneous pasting theorem needs only
+  the two forward marginal comparisons, so the saved unused second joint
+  family and its extra comparison were omitted. Its error function still
+  satisfies the same polynomial contract.
+- `XEvalDeficit` and `SubLineXDeficit` recover only the opposite-placement
+  X estimates needed from saved `EvalDeficit` and `SubLineDeficit`. The saved
+  XZ ordered-point estimate is added alongside the existing ZX estimate.
+- `ExtendedLines/Measurement`, `Overlap`, and `Estimates` recover the
+  conditional law, affine polynomial construction, degree support, and
+  two-placement real-part overlap estimates from saved `Apply.lean`.
+- The two scalar estimates `rpow_quarter_nonneg` and `sqrt_deficit_bound_le`,
+  which the recovered estimates share with the claims module, are stated in
+  `Combining/ErrorBounds.lean` with the other formalization-only scalar
+  bounds; neither is specific to Claims 17-1 through 17-3.
+- The saved established-error construction is inlined into the target.
+  Its universal outer constant remains `1`. No narrower helper replaces the
+  current `exists_extendedLinesWitness_established_ofPointsWitness`: that
+  obligation quantifies arbitrary scalar point errors, whereas the saved
+  helper first fixes a polynomially controlled point family. Its signature
+  and proof hole are left unchanged.
+
+### Statement integrity
+
+Paper assumptions: an admissible parameter tuple and a projective strategy
+passing the Pauli basis test with error epsilon; the preceding construction
+supplies the joint point measurements.
+
+Lean assumptions: the existing `AdmissibleParams` and `ProjectiveSetting`
+domain. The point witness and its polynomial error are constructed
+existentially. No new bridge premise, positivity premise, axiom, or proof
+hole is added.
+
+Paper conclusion: two extended-line consistency comparisons, axis degree at
+most d, general degree at most md+1, source line-point sampling, field answers,
+and the printed error `poly(m^2 * epsilon, md/q)`.

+Lean conclusion: the unchanged directly indexed `ExtendedLinesWitness`, both
+opposite-placement comparisons on completed answers, the same degree bounds,

    27	/-- A positive atom gives a positive atom of every push-forward. -/
    28	private theorem map_weight_pos_of_weight_pos {Source Target : Type*}
    29	    [DecidableEq Target] (law : Distribution Source) (mapping : Source → Target)
    30	    (sample : Source) (hpositive : 0 < law.weight sample) :
    31	    0 < (law.map mapping).weight (mapping sample) := by
    32	  classical
    33	  have hmem : sample ∈ law.support := by
    34	    by_contra hnot
    35	    simp [law.outsideSupport sample hnot] at hpositive
    36	  exact hpositive.trans_le (Finset.single_le_sum
    37	    (fun other _ => law.nonnegative other) (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨hmem, rfl⟩))

    39	/-- Every canonical direct line has positive marginal mass. In particular, the
    40	conditional distribution in the construction at paper lines 1118--1132 is defined
    41	on every direct line, including zero-direction diagonal lines. -/
    42	theorem directLinePointDist_line_weight_pos (params : DirectLdParams)
    43	    (line : DirectLineDesc params) :
    44	    0 < ((directLinePointDist params).map Prod.fst).weight line := by
    45	  have huniform (sample : DirectLdSpace params) :
    46	      0 < (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace params)).weight sample := by
    47	    rw [uniformDistribution_weight_apply]
    48	    positivity
    49	  suffices hpoint : 0 < (directLinePointDist params).weight (line, line.base) by
    50	    exact map_weight_pos_of_weight_pos _ Prod.fst _ hpoint
    51	  cases line with
    52	  | axis base index baseFixed =>
    53	    let sample : DirectLdSpace params := ⟨base, index, 0⟩
    54	    have haxis := map_weight_pos_of_weight_pos
    55	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace params))
    56	      (fun source => (directALineDescOf params source, source.point)) sample (huniform sample)
    57	    have hdecode : directALineDescOf params sample = .axis base index baseFixed := by
    58	      simp [directALineDescOf, sample, baseFixed]
    59	    change 0 < (directALinePointDist params).weight _ at haxis
    60	    rw [hdecode] at haxis
    61	    have hother := (directDLinePointDist params).nonnegative
    62	      (DirectLineDesc.axis base index baseFixed, base)
    63	    change 0 < (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (directALinePointDist params).weight _ +
    64	      (1 - 1 / 2) * (directDLinePointDist params).weight _
    65	    change 0 < (directALinePointDist params).weight
    66	      (DirectLineDesc.axis base index baseFixed, base) at haxis
    67	    dsimp only [DirectLineDesc.base]
    68	    linarith
    69	  | diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero =>
    70	    let sample : DirectLdSpace params := ⟨base, index, direction⟩
    71	    have hprefix : directPrefixProjection index direction = direction := by
    72	      funext coordinate
    73	      simp only [directPrefixProjection]
    74	      split_ifs with hbefore
    75	      · exact (prefixZero coordinate hbefore).symm
    76	      · rfl
    77	    have hdiagonal := map_weight_pos_of_weight_pos
    78	      (uniformDistribution (DirectLdSpace params))
    79	      (fun source => (directDLineDescOf params source, source.point)) sample (huniform sample)
    80	    have hdecode : directDLineDescOf params sample =
    81	        .diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero := by
    82	      simp [directDLineDescOf, sample, hprefix, baseFixed]
    83	    change 0 < (directDLinePointDist params).weight _ at hdiagonal
    84	    rw [hdecode] at hdiagonal
    85	    have hother := (directALinePointDist params).nonnegative
    86	      (DirectLineDesc.diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero, base)
    87	    change 0 < (1 / 2 : ℝ) * (directALinePointDist params).weight _ +
    88	      (1 - 1 / 2) * (directDLinePointDist params).weight _
    89	    change 0 < (directDLinePointDist params).weight
    90	      (DirectLineDesc.diagonal base index direction baseFixed prefixZero, base) at hdiagonal
    91	    dsimp only [DirectLineDesc.base]
    92	    linarith

    94	/-- The supported triples over a fixed extended line. Restricting the carrier
    95	retains the affine compatibility proof without choosing any substitute lines. -/
    96	abbrev SubLineWitness.Fiber {params : AdmissibleParams} (sublines : SubLineWitness params)
    97	    (line : DirectLineDesc params.extendedDirectLd) :=
    98	  ↥(sublines.D.support.filter (fun sample => sample.1 = line))

   100	/-- The mass of a subline fiber is positive by the prescribed extended marginal. -/
   101	theorem SubLineWitness.fiber_mass_pos {params : AdmissibleParams}
   102	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (line : DirectLineDesc params.extendedDirectLd) :
   103	    0 < (sublines.D.map Prod.fst).weight line := by
   104	  rw [sublines.extended_marginal]
   105	  exact directLinePointDist_line_weight_pos _ _

   107	/-- The genuine conditional law of the supported subline triples given their
   108	extended line, as in paper lines 1118--1132. Every extended line has positive
   109	marginal mass. -/
   110	def SubLineWitness.conditionalLaw {params : AdmissibleParams}
   111	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (line : DirectLineDesc params.extendedDirectLd) :
   112	    Distribution (sublines.Fiber line) where
   113	  support := Finset.univ
   114	  weight sample := sublines.D.weight sample.val / (sublines.D.map Prod.fst).weight line
   115	  nonnegative sample := div_nonneg (sublines.D.nonnegative sample.val)
   116	    (sublines.fiber_mass_pos line).le
   117	  outsideSupport sample hnot := (hnot (Finset.mem_univ sample)).elim

   119	/-- Conditioning on an extended line preserves total mass one. -/
   120	theorem SubLineWitness.conditionalLaw_isProbability {params : AdmissibleParams}
   121	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (line : DirectLineDesc params.extendedDirectLd) :
   122	    (sublines.conditionalLaw line).IsProbability := by
   123	  change (∑ sample : sublines.Fiber line,
   124	    sublines.D.weight sample.val / (sublines.D.map Prod.fst).weight line) = 1
   125	  rw [← Finset.sum_div, Finset.sum_coe_sort]
   126	  exact div_self (sublines.fiber_mass_pos line).ne'

   128	/-- Supported subline triples supply all eight affine coordinates in the
   129	polynomial combination formula; the choice is only of proved compatible data. -/
   130	private theorem SubLineWitness.exists_affineData {params : AdmissibleParams}
   131	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (sample : SubLineTriple params)
   132	    (hsample : sample ∈ sublines.D.support) :
   133	    ∃ data : Fin 8 → PauliScalar params,
   134	      IsCombineLineCompatible (directPointToPauli params sample.1.base)
   135	        (directPointToPauli params sample.1.direction)
   136	        sample.2.1.base sample.2.1.direction sample.2.2.base sample.2.2.direction
   137	        (data 0) (data 1) (data 2) (data 3) (data 4) (data 5) (data 6) (data 7) := by
   138	  obtain ⟨offsetX, slopeX, offsetZ, slopeZ, alpha, alphaSlope, beta, betaSlope, hcompat⟩ :=
   139	    sublines.compatibility sample hsample
   140	  exact ⟨![offsetX, slopeX, offsetZ, slopeZ, alpha, alphaSlope, beta, betaSlope], hcompat⟩

   148	/-- The selected coordinates satisfy the source's affine line identities. -/
   149	theorem SubLineWitness.affineData_compatible {params : AdmissibleParams}
   150	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (sample : SubLineTriple params)
   151	    (hsample : sample ∈ sublines.D.support) :
   152	    let data := sublines.affineData sample hsample
   153	    IsCombineLineCompatible (directPointToPauli params sample.1.base)
   154	      (directPointToPauli params sample.1.direction)
   155	      sample.2.1.base sample.2.1.direction sample.2.2.base sample.2.2.direction
   156	      (data 0) (data 1) (data 2) (data 3) (data 4) (data 5) (data 6) (data 7) :=
   157	  Classical.choose_spec (sublines.exists_affineData sample hsample)

   159	/-- The source polynomial combination on a supported triple, transported only
   160	along the canonical identification of the two scalar models. -/
   161	def SubLineWitness.combinedPolynomial {params : AdmissibleParams}
   162	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (sample : SubLineTriple params)
   163	    (hsample : sample ∈ sublines.D.support)
   164	    (polynomials : DegPoly params.toLdParams (params.m * params.d) ×
   165	      DegPoly params.toLdParams (params.m * params.d)) :
   166	    DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd (params.m * params.d + 1) :=
   167	  let data := sublines.affineData sample hsample
   168	  fun index => (extendedDirectScalarEquiv params).symm
   169	    (combineLinePoly (data 0) (data 1) (data 2) (data 3)
   170	      (data 4) (data 5) (data 6) (data 7) polynomials.1 polynomials.2 index)

   172	/-- The directly indexed form of the extended-line POVM at paper lines
   173	1118--1132: condition the subline law and average the postprocessed paired-line POVMs. -/
   174	def SubLineWitness.extendedMeasurement {params : AdmissibleParams}
   175	    {error pointError lineError : ℝ} {setting : ProjectiveSetting params error}
   176	    {points : CombinedPointsWitness setting pointError}
   177	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (lines : CombinedLinesWitness setting points lineError)
   178	    (side : PlayerSide) (line : DirectLineDesc params.extendedDirectLd) :
   179	    Quantum.Measurement (DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd (params.m * params.d + 1))
   180	      (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace side) := by
   181	  let family (sample : sublines.Fiber line) :=
   182	    (lines.T side sample.val.2.1 sample.val.2.2).postprocess
   183	      (sublines.combinedPolynomial sample.val (Finset.mem_filter.mp sample.property).1)
   184	  have hsum : (∑ polynomial, averageOperatorOverDistribution (sublines.conditionalLaw line)
   185	      (fun sample => (family sample).effect polynomial)) = 1 := by
   186	    rw [← averageOperatorOverDistribution_sum]
   187	    simp only [Quantum.Measurement.sum_eq_one]
   188	    exact averageOperatorOverDistribution_const_of_isProbability _
   189	      (sublines.conditionalLaw_isProbability line) 1
   190	  exact { effect := fun polynomial => averageOperatorOverDistribution
   191	            (sublines.conditionalLaw line) (fun sample => (family sample).effect polynomial)
   192	          pos := fun polynomial => averageOperatorOverDistribution_nonneg _ _
   193	            (fun sample => (family sample).pos polynomial)
   194	          sum_le_one := le_of_eq hsum
   195	          sum_eq_one := hsum }

   197	/-- Integrating the conditional law recovers the original subline law.
   198	This is finite disintegration, not an independence assertion about projections. -/
   199	theorem SubLineWitness.avgOver_conditionalLaw {params : AdmissibleParams}
   200	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (quantity : SubLineTriple params → ℝ) :
   201	    avgOver (sublines.D.map Prod.fst) (fun line =>
   202	      avgOver (sublines.conditionalLaw line) (fun sample => quantity sample.val)) =
   203	        avgOver sublines.D quantity := by
   204	  classical
   205	  simp only [avgOver, SubLineWitness.conditionalLaw]
   206	  calc
   207	    (∑ line ∈ (sublines.D.map Prod.fst).support,
   208	        (sublines.D.map Prod.fst).weight line *
   209	          ∑ sample : sublines.Fiber line,
   210	            (sublines.D.weight sample.val / (sublines.D.map Prod.fst).weight line) *
   211	              quantity sample.val) =
   212	        ∑ line ∈ (sublines.D.map Prod.fst).support,
   213	          ∑ sample ∈ sublines.D.support.filter (fun sample => sample.1 = line),
   214	            sublines.D.weight sample * quantity sample := by
   215	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   216	      intro line _
   217	      rw [Finset.mul_sum]
   218	      trans ∑ sample : sublines.Fiber line, sublines.D.weight sample.val * quantity sample.val
   219	      · apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   220	        intro sample _
   221	        field_simp [(sublines.fiber_mass_pos line).ne']
   222	        exact (div_eq_iff (sublines.fiber_mass_pos line).ne').mpr (by ring)
   223	      · exact Finset.sum_coe_sort
   224	          (sublines.D.support.filter (fun sample => sample.1 = line))
   225	          (fun sample => sublines.D.weight sample * quantity sample)
   226	    _ = ∑ sample ∈ sublines.D.support, sublines.D.weight sample * quantity sample := by
   227	      exact Finset.sum_fiberwise_of_maps_to
   228	        (fun sample hsample => Finset.mem_image.mpr ⟨sample, hsample, rfl⟩) _

   230	/-- A determined direct evaluation gives precisely its completed answer. -/
   231	private theorem directEvalOpt_eq_some_of_evaluatesTo {params : DirectLdParams} {bound : ℕ}
   232	    (line : DirectLineDesc params) (polynomial : DirectDegPoly params bound)
   233	    (point : Fin params.m → DirectScalarQ params) (value : DirectScalarQ params)
   234	    (heval : DirectEvaluatesTo line polynomial point value) :
   235	    directEvalOpt line point polynomial = some value := by
   236	  classical
   237	  have hexists : ∃ answer, DirectEvaluatesTo line polynomial point answer := ⟨value, heval⟩
   238	  rw [directEvalOpt, dif_pos hexists]
   239	  obtain ⟨parameter, hparameter⟩ := heval.1
   240	  exact congrArg some (((Classical.choose_spec hexists).2 parameter hparameter).symm.trans
   241	    (heval.2 parameter hparameter))

   243	/-- Evaluation commutes with the canonical scalar identification. -/
   244	private theorem evalCoefficient_extendedScalar {params : AdmissibleParams} {bound : ℕ}
   245	    (polynomial : DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd bound)
   246	    (parameter : DirectScalarQ params.extendedDirectLd) :
   247	    extendedDirectScalarEquiv params (evalCoefficient polynomial parameter) =
   248	      evalCoefficient (fun index => extendedDirectScalarEquiv params (polynomial index))
   249	        (extendedDirectScalarEquiv params parameter) := by
   250	  simp [evalCoefficient]

   252	/-- If both projected polynomials have determined values, their actual combined
   253	polynomial has the required determined value at the extended point. This also
   254	covers zero-direction lines: every parameter is checked, rather than selecting
   255	one parameter or assigning an arbitrary field value. -/
   256	theorem SubLineWitness.combinedPolynomial_evaluatesTo {params : AdmissibleParams}
   257	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (sample : SubLineTriple params)
   258	    (hsample : sample ∈ sublines.D.support)
   259	    (polynomials : DegPoly params.toLdParams (params.m * params.d) ×
   260	      DegPoly params.toLdParams (params.m * params.d))
   261	    (point : Fin params.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ params.extendedDirectLd)
   262	    (hpoint : point ∈ sample.1.pointSet) (valueX valueZ : PauliScalar params)
   263	    (hevalX : EvaluatesTo sample.2.1 polynomials.1
   264	      (projX (directPointToPauli params point)) valueX)
   265	    (hevalZ : EvaluatesTo sample.2.2 polynomials.2
   266	      (projZ (directPointToPauli params point)) valueZ) :
   267	    DirectEvaluatesTo sample.1 (sublines.combinedPolynomial sample hsample polynomials) point
   268	      ((extendedDirectScalarEquiv params).symm
   269	        ((directPointToPauli params point) (alphaVar params.m) * valueX +
   270	          (directPointToPauli params point) (betaVar params.m) * valueZ)) := by
   271	  obtain ⟨initialParameter, hinitial⟩ := hpoint
   272	  refine ⟨⟨initialParameter, hinitial⟩, ?_⟩
   273	  intro parameter hparameter
   274	  let data := sublines.affineData sample hsample
   275	  have hcompat := sublines.affineData_compatible sample hsample
   276	  have hformula := combineLinePoly_spec
   277	    (directPointToPauli params sample.1.base) (directPointToPauli params sample.1.direction)
   278	    sample.2.1.base sample.2.1.direction sample.2.2.base sample.2.2.direction
   279	    (data 0) (data 1) (data 2) (data 3) (data 4) (data 5) (data 6) (data 7)
   280	    polynomials.1 polynomials.2 hcompat (extendedDirectScalarEquiv params parameter)
   281	  have hpointTransport : directPointToPauli params point =
   282	      directPointToPauli params sample.1.base +
   283	        extendedDirectScalarEquiv params parameter •
   284	          directPointToPauli params sample.1.direction := by
   285	    rw [hparameter, directPointToPauli_add, directPointToPauli_smul]
   286	  have hvalueX := hevalX.2 _ (hpointTransport ▸ hformula.1)
   287	  have hvalueZ := hevalZ.2 _ (hpointTransport ▸ hformula.2.1)
   288	  apply (extendedDirectScalarEquiv params).injective
   289	  rw [evalCoefficient_extendedScalar, RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
   290	  simp only [SubLineWitness.combinedPolynomial, RingEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
   291	  rw [hformula.2.2]
   292	  erw [hvalueX, hvalueZ]
   293	  rw [hpointTransport]
   294	  simp only [Pi.add_apply, Pi.smul_apply, smul_eq_mul]
   295	  rw [hcompat.1, hcompat.2.1, hcompat.2.2.1, hcompat.2.2.2.1]
   296	
   297	/-- Completed evaluation of the actual combination agrees with the source
   298	linear combination whenever both source evaluations are defined. -/
   299	theorem SubLineWitness.combinedPolynomial_evalOpt {params : AdmissibleParams}
   300	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (sample : SubLineTriple params)
   301	    (hsample : sample ∈ sublines.D.support)
   302	    (polynomials : DegPoly params.toLdParams (params.m * params.d) ×
   303	      DegPoly params.toLdParams (params.m * params.d))
   304	    (point : Fin params.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ params.extendedDirectLd)
   305	    (hpoint : point ∈ sample.1.pointSet) (valueX valueZ : PauliScalar params)
   306	    (hevalX : evalOpt sample.2.1 (projX (directPointToPauli params point)) polynomials.1 =
   307	      some valueX)
   308	    (hevalZ : evalOpt sample.2.2 (projZ (directPointToPauli params point)) polynomials.2 =
   309	      some valueZ) :
   310	    (directEvalOpt sample.1 point (sublines.combinedPolynomial sample hsample polynomials)).map
   311	      (extendedDirectScalarEquiv params) =
   312	        some ((directPointToPauli params point) (alphaVar params.m) * valueX +
   313	          (directPointToPauli params point) (betaVar params.m) * valueZ) := by
   314	  rw [directEvalOpt_eq_some_of_evaluatesTo _ _ _ _
   315	    (sublines.combinedPolynomial_evaluatesTo sample hsample polynomials point hpoint valueX valueZ
   316	      ((evalOpt_eq_some_iff _ _ _ _).mp hevalX) ((evalOpt_eq_some_iff _ _ _ _).mp hevalZ))]
   317	  simp

   319	/-- Coefficient support bounds the degree of the represented polynomial. -/
   320	private theorem linePolynomial_natDegree_le_of_coefficients {Scalar : Type*}
   321	    [Field Scalar] {bound degree : ℕ} (polynomial : Fin (bound + 1) → Scalar)
   322	    (hdegree : ∀ index, degree < index.val → polynomial index = 0) :
   323	    (linePolynomialOfCoefficients polynomial).natDegree ≤ degree := by
   324	  apply Polynomial.natDegree_sum_le_of_forall_le
   325	  intro index _
   326	  by_cases hindex : index.val ≤ degree
   327	  · refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
   328	    have hpower := Polynomial.natDegree_pow_le
   329	      (p := (Polynomial.X : Polynomial Scalar)) (n := index.val)
   330	    simp only [Polynomial.natDegree_X, Nat.mul_one] at hpower
   331	    simpa using hpower.trans hindex
   332	  · simp [hdegree index (Nat.lt_of_not_ge hindex)]
   333	
   334	/-- Affine substitution preserves a degree bound. -/
   335	private theorem affine_comp_natDegree_le {Scalar : Type*} [Field Scalar]
   336	    (polynomial : Polynomial Scalar) (offset slope : Scalar) {degree : ℕ}
   337	    (hdegree : polynomial.natDegree ≤ degree) :
   338	    (polynomial.comp (Polynomial.C offset + Polynomial.C slope * Polynomial.X)).natDegree ≤
   339	      degree := by
   340	  have haffine : (Polynomial.C offset + Polynomial.C slope * Polynomial.X).natDegree ≤ 1 := by
   341	    refine (Polynomial.natDegree_add_le _ _).trans (max_le ?_ ?_)
   342	    · simp
   343	    · exact Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans (by simp)
   344	  exact Polynomial.natDegree_comp_le.trans (by simpa using Nat.mul_le_mul hdegree haffine)
   345	
   346	/-- The source combination has degree at most `degree` on an axis line:
   347	either the two scalar coordinates are constant, or both projected parameters
   348	are constant. This is the algebraic assertion at paper lines 1127--1132. -/
   349	theorem combineLinePoly_axis_degree {Scalar : Type*} [Field Scalar] {bound degree : ℕ}
   350	    (hdegree : 1 ≤ degree) (data : Fin 8 → Scalar)
   351	    (polynomialX polynomialZ : Fin (bound + 1) → Scalar)
   352	    (hdegreeX : ∀ index, degree < index.val → polynomialX index = 0)
   353	    (hdegreeZ : ∀ index, degree < index.val → polynomialZ index = 0)
   354	    (haxis : (data 5 = 0 ∧ data 7 = 0) ∨ (data 1 = 0 ∧ data 3 = 0)) :
   355	    ∀ index : Fin (bound + 1 + 1), degree < index.val →
   356	      combineLinePoly (data 0) (data 1) (data 2) (data 3)
   357	        (data 4) (data 5) (data 6) (data 7) polynomialX polynomialZ index = 0 := by
   358	  have hpolyX := linePolynomial_natDegree_le_of_coefficients polynomialX hdegreeX
   359	  have hpolyZ := linePolynomial_natDegree_le_of_coefficients polynomialZ hdegreeZ
   360	  have htotal : (combineLinePolynomial (data 0) (data 1) (data 2) (data 3)
   361	      (data 4) (data 5) (data 6) (data 7) polynomialX polynomialZ).natDegree ≤ degree := by
   362	    unfold combineLinePolynomial
   363	    rcases haxis with ⟨halpha, hbeta⟩ | ⟨hparamX, hparamZ⟩
   364	    · simp only [halpha, hbeta, Polynomial.C_0, zero_mul, add_zero]
   365	      refine (Polynomial.natDegree_add_le _ _).trans (max_le ?_ ?_)
   366	      · refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
   367	        simpa only [Polynomial.natDegree_C, Nat.zero_add] using
   368	          (affine_comp_natDegree_le _ (data 0) (data 1) hpolyX)
   369	      · refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
   370	        simpa only [Polynomial.natDegree_C, Nat.zero_add] using
   371	          (affine_comp_natDegree_le _ (data 2) (data 3) hpolyZ)
   372	    · simp only [hparamX, hparamZ, Polynomial.C_0, zero_mul, add_zero, Polynomial.comp_C]
   373	      have hterm (constant slope value : Scalar) :
   374	          ((Polynomial.C constant + Polynomial.C slope * Polynomial.X) *
   375	            Polynomial.C value).natDegree ≤ degree := by
   376	        refine Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans ?_
   377	        simp only [Polynomial.natDegree_C, Nat.add_zero]
   378	        exact (Polynomial.natDegree_add_le _ _).trans (max_le (by simp)
   379	          (Polynomial.natDegree_mul_le.trans (by simpa using hdegree)))

   394	/-- Two equal points on a nonzero affine direction force the parameter slope to vanish. -/
   395	private theorem affine_slope_eq_zero {Scalar : Type*} [Field Scalar] {dimension : ℕ}
   396	    {point base direction : Fin dimension → Scalar} {offset slope : Scalar}
   397	    (hdirection : direction ≠ 0) (hzero : point = base + offset • direction)
   398	    (hone : point = base + (offset + slope) • direction) : slope = 0 := by
   399	  have hequal := add_left_cancel (hzero.symm.trans hone)
   400	  have hvanish : slope • direction = 0 := by
   401	    apply add_left_cancel (a := offset • direction)
   402	    simpa only [add_smul, add_zero] using hequal.symm
   403	  exact (smul_eq_zero.mp hvanish).resolve_right hdirection

   405	/-- Axis subline coordinates satisfy the source's constant-coordinate alternative. -/
   406	theorem SubLineWitness.affineData_axis {params : AdmissibleParams}
   407	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (sample : SubLineTriple params)
   408	    (hsample : sample ∈ sublines.D.support) (haxis : sample.1.kind = .axis) :
   409	    let data := sublines.affineData sample hsample
   410	    (data 5 = 0 ∧ data 7 = 0) ∨ (data 1 = 0 ∧ data 3 = 0) := by
   411	  let data := sublines.affineData sample hsample
   412	  have hcompat := sublines.affineData_compatible sample hsample
   413	  have hsource := sublines.axis_closure sample hsample haxis
   414	  have hcoordinate : directPointToPauli params sample.1.direction =
   415	      coordinateDirection sample.1.index := by
   416	    rcases sample with ⟨line, pair⟩
   417	    cases line with
   418	    | axis => exact directPointToPauli_coordinateDirection params _
   419	    | diagonal => cases haxis
   420	  by_cases hspecial : sample.1.index = alphaVar params.m ∨ sample.1.index = betaVar params.m
   421	  · right
   422	    have hprojection : projX (directPointToPauli params sample.1.direction) = 0 ∧
   423	        projZ (directPointToPauli params sample.1.direction) = 0 := by
   424	      rw [hcoordinate]
   425	      rcases hspecial with halpha | hbeta
   426	      · rw [halpha]
   427	        exact ⟨projX_coordinateDirection_alphaVar, projZ_coordinateDirection_alphaVar⟩
   428	      · rw [hbeta]
   429	        exact ⟨projX_coordinateDirection_betaVar, projZ_coordinateDirection_betaVar⟩
   430	    have hzero := hcompat.2.2.2.2 (0 : PauliScalar params)
   431	    have hone := hcompat.2.2.2.2 (1 : PauliScalar params)
   432	    simp only [zero_smul, add_zero, mul_zero] at hzero
   433	    simp only [one_smul, mul_one, projX_add, projZ_add, hprojection.1, hprojection.2,
   434	      add_zero] at hone
   435	    exact ⟨affine_slope_eq_zero (Scalar := PauliScalar params)
   436	      (source_axis_direction_ne_zero _ hsource.1) hzero.1 hone.1,
   437	      affine_slope_eq_zero (Scalar := PauliScalar params)
   438	        (source_axis_direction_ne_zero _ hsource.2) hzero.2 hone.2⟩
   439	  · left
   440	    have halpha := Ne.symm (not_or.mp hspecial).1
   441	    have hbeta := Ne.symm (not_or.mp hspecial).2
   442	    rw [← hcompat.2.1, ← hcompat.2.2.2.1, hcoordinate]
   443	    simp [coordinateDirection, halpha, hbeta]

   448	    (hsample : sample ∈ sublines.D.support) (haxis : sample.1.kind = .axis)

   451	    (hdegreeX : polynomials.1.FitsDegree params.d)
   452	    (hdegreeZ : polynomials.2.FitsDegree params.d) :

   454	      sublines.combinedPolynomial sample hsample polynomials index = 0 := by
   455	  intro index hindex

   457	    polynomials.1 polynomials.2 hdegreeX hdegreeZ
   458	    (sublines.affineData_axis sample hsample haxis) index hindex

   463	/-- The conditional average of the actual paired-line POVMs has no outcomes
   464	above degree `d` on an extended axis line, as asserted at paper lines 1127--1132. -/
   465	theorem SubLineWitness.extendedMeasurement_axis_degree {params : AdmissibleParams}
   466	    {error pointError lineError : ℝ} {setting : ProjectiveSetting params error}
   467	    {points : CombinedPointsWitness setting pointError}
   468	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (lines : CombinedLinesWitness setting points lineError)
   469	    (side : PlayerSide) (line : DirectLineDesc params.extendedDirectLd)
   470	    (polynomial : DirectDegPoly params.extendedDirectLd (params.m * params.d + 1))
   471	    (haxis : line.kind = .axis) (hdegree : ¬ ∀ index, params.d < index.val → polynomial index = 0) :
   472	    (sublines.extendedMeasurement lines side line).effect polynomial = 0 := by
   473	  classical
   474	  change averageOperatorOverDistribution (sublines.conditionalLaw line) (fun sample =>
   475	    ((lines.T side sample.val.2.1 sample.val.2.2).postprocess
   476	      (sublines.combinedPolynomial sample.val
   477	        (Finset.mem_filter.mp sample.property).1)).effect polynomial) = 0
   478	  unfold averageOperatorOverDistribution
   479	  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   480	  intro sample _
   481	  have hsample := (Finset.mem_filter.mp sample.property).1
   482	  have hsampleAxis : sample.val.1.kind = .axis := by
   483	    rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp sample.property).2]
   484	    exact haxis
   485	  have hsource := sublines.axis_closure sample.val hsample hsampleAxis
   486	  suffices hzero : ((lines.T side sample.val.2.1 sample.val.2.2).postprocess
   487	      (sublines.combinedPolynomial sample.val hsample)).effect polynomial = 0 by
   488	    exact (congrArg (fun operator => (sublines.conditionalLaw line).weight sample • operator)
   489	      hzero).trans (smul_zero _)
   490	  rw [Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
   491	  apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
   492	  intro pair hpair
   493	  by_cases hdegreeX : pair.1.FitsDegree params.d
   494	  · by_cases hdegreeZ : pair.2.FitsDegree params.d
   495	    · have hfit := sublines.combinedPolynomial_axis_degree sample.val hsample hsampleAxis
   496	        pair hdegreeX hdegreeZ
   497	      rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp hpair).2] at hfit
   498	      exact (hdegree hfit).elim
   499	    · exact lines.axis_degree_Z side _ _ _ _ hsource.2 hdegreeZ
   500	  · exact lines.axis_degree_X side _ _ _ _ hsource.1 hdegreeX

    28	/-- The completed point-pair effect is bounded by the effect of its linear
    29	combination at the actual combined evaluation. Undefined source evaluations
    30	contribute zero on the point side. The statement holds for either player's
    31	measurement without any symmetry assumption on the strategy or local spaces. -/
    32	theorem SubLineWitness.completedPoint_effect_le {params : AdmissibleParams}
    33	    {Carrier : Type*} [Fintype Carrier] [DecidableEq Carrier]
    34	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (sample : SubLineTriple params)
    35	    (hsample : sample ∈ sublines.D.support)
    36	    (polynomials : DegPoly params.toLdParams (params.m * params.d) ×
    37	      DegPoly params.toLdParams (params.m * params.d))
    38	    (point : Fin params.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ params.extendedDirectLd)
    39	    (hpoint : point ∈ sample.1.pointSet)
    40	    (measurement : Quantum.Measurement (PauliScalar params × PauliScalar params) Carrier) :
    41	    (measurement.postprocess (fun pair => (some pair.1, some pair.2))).effect
    42	      (evalOpt sample.2.1 (projX (directPointToPauli params point)) polynomials.1,
    43	        evalOpt sample.2.2 (projZ (directPointToPauli params point)) polynomials.2) ≤
    44	      (measurement.postprocess (fun pair => some
    45	        ((directPointToPauli params point) (alphaVar params.m) * pair.1 +
    46	          (directPointToPauli params point) (betaVar params.m) * pair.2))).effect
    47	        ((directEvalOpt sample.1 point
    48	          (sublines.combinedPolynomial sample hsample polynomials)).map
    49	            (extendedDirectScalarEquiv params)) := by
    50	  classical
    51	  have hnoneX (value : Option (PauliScalar params)) :
    52	      (measurement.postprocess (fun pair => (some pair.1, some pair.2))).effect (none, value) =
    53	        0 := by
    54	    rw [Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
    55	    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    56	    intro pair hpair
    57	    have himpossible := congrArg Prod.fst (Finset.mem_filter.mp hpair).2
    58	    simp at himpossible
    59	  have hnoneZ (value : Option (PauliScalar params)) :
    60	      (measurement.postprocess (fun pair => (some pair.1, some pair.2))).effect (value, none) =
    61	        0 := by
    62	    rw [Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
    63	    apply Finset.sum_eq_zero
    64	    intro pair hpair
    65	    have himpossible := congrArg Prod.snd (Finset.mem_filter.mp hpair).2
    66	    simp at himpossible
    67	  cases hevalX : evalOpt sample.2.1 (projX (directPointToPauli params point)) polynomials.1 with
    68	  | none =>
    69	    erw [hnoneX]
    70	    exact Quantum.Submeasurement.pos _ _
    71	  | some valueX =>
    72	    cases hevalZ : evalOpt sample.2.2 (projZ (directPointToPauli params point)) polynomials.2 with
    73	    | none =>
    74	      erw [hnoneZ]
    75	      exact Quantum.Submeasurement.pos _ _
    76	    | some valueZ =>
    77	      rw [sublines.combinedPolynomial_evalOpt sample hsample polynomials point hpoint
    78	        valueX valueZ hevalX hevalZ]
    79	      have hinjective : Function.Injective
    80	          (fun pair : PauliScalar params × PauliScalar params => (some pair.1, some pair.2)) := by
    81	        intro left right hequal
    82	        exact Prod.ext (Option.some.inj (congrArg Prod.fst hequal))
    83	          (Option.some.inj (congrArg Prod.snd hequal))
    84	      erw [SandwichProduct.postprocess_effect_of_injective measurement _ hinjective
    85	        (valueX, valueZ)]
    86	      rw [Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect]
    87	      exact Finset.single_le_sum (fun pair _ => measurement.pos pair)
    88	        (Finset.mem_filter.mpr ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, rfl⟩)

   146	/-- A placed overlap is linear in an averaged left operator. -/
   147	private theorem placed_overlap_average {params : AdmissibleParams} {error : ℝ}
   148	    {Sample : Type*} (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error) (first second : Placement)
   149	    (law : Distribution Sample) (family : Sample → Op (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace first.side))
   150	    (right : Op (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace second.side)) :
   151	    stateQForm setting.psiHat
   152	      (setting.place first (averageOperatorOverDistribution law family) *
   153	        setting.place second right) =
   154	      avgOver law (fun sample => stateQForm setting.psiHat
   155	        (setting.place first (family sample) * setting.place second right)) := by
   156	  unfold averageOperatorOverDistribution avgOver
   157	  rw [setting.place_finsetSum, Finset.sum_mul, stateQForm_finset_sum]
   158	  apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   159	  intro sample _
   160	  rw [place_real_smul, smul_mul_assoc]
   161	  have hscalar (operator : Op (SixReg params setting.toStrategy.ιA setting.toStrategy.ιB)) :
   162	      law.weight sample • operator = (law.weight sample : ℂ) • operator := by
   163	    ext row column
   164	    simp [Complex.real_smul]
   165	  rw [hscalar]
   166	  simp only [stateQForm, WinImplications.applyOperatorToState_smul_op, inner_smul_right,
   167	    Complex.mul_re, Complex.ofReal_re, Complex.ofReal_im, zero_mul, sub_zero]

   169	/-- Postprocessing the left measurement groups, but does not alter, its overlap
   170	with a family indexed by the postprocessed answer. -/
   171	private theorem placed_overlap_postprocess {params : AdmissibleParams} {error : ℝ}
   172	    {Answer Output : Type*} [Fintype Answer] [DecidableEq Answer]
   173	    [Fintype Output] [DecidableEq Output]
   174	    (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error) (first second : Placement)
   175	    (measurement : Quantum.Measurement Answer (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace first.side))
   176	    (mapping : Answer → Output) (right : Output → Op (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace second.side)) :
   177	    (∑ output, stateQForm setting.psiHat
   178	      (setting.place first ((measurement.postprocess mapping).effect output) *
   179	        setting.place second (right output))) =
   180	      ∑ answer, stateQForm setting.psiHat
   181	        (setting.place first (measurement.effect answer) *
   182	          setting.place second (right (mapping answer))) := by
   183	  classical
   184	  simp only [Quantum.Measurement.postprocess_effect, setting.place_finsetSum,
   185	    Finset.sum_mul, stateQForm_finset_sum]
   186	  calc
   187	    (∑ output, ∑ answer ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer => mapping answer = output),
   188	        stateQForm setting.psiHat (setting.place first (measurement.effect answer) *
   189	          setting.place second (right output))) =
   190	        ∑ output, ∑ answer ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun answer => mapping answer = output),
   191	          stateQForm setting.psiHat (setting.place first (measurement.effect answer) *
   192	            setting.place second (right (mapping answer))) := by
   193	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   194	      intro output _
   195	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
   196	      intro answer hanswer
   197	      rw [(Finset.mem_filter.mp hanswer).2]
   198	    _ = _ := Finset.sum_fiberwise _ _ _

   201	effect. This applies to both directed player placements without exchanging spaces. -/
   202	private theorem placed_overlap_mono {params : AdmissibleParams} {error : ℝ}
   203	    (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error) (first second : Placement)
   204	    (hopposite : first.IsOpposite second)
   205	    (left : Op (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace first.side))
   206	    (lower upper : Op (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace second.side))
   207	    (hleft : 0 ≤ left) (hright : lower ≤ upper) :

   209	      stateQForm setting.psiHat (setting.place first left * setting.place second upper) := by
   210	  have hpositive := setting.place_mul_place_nonneg first second hopposite hleft
   211	    (sub_nonneg.mpr hright)

   213	  exact quadratic_form_mono (sub_nonneg.mp hpositive) setting.psiHat

   215	/-- Expand the actual conditional extended-line POVM in a placed overlap.
   216	This is exactly the averaging step at paper lines 1118--1134. -/
   217	theorem SubLineWitness.extendedMeasurement_overlap {params : AdmissibleParams}
   218	    {error pointError lineError : ℝ} {setting : ProjectiveSetting params error}
   219	    {points : CombinedPointsWitness setting pointError}
   220	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (lines : CombinedLinesWitness setting points lineError)
   221	    (first second : Placement) (line : DirectLineDesc params.extendedDirectLd)
   222	    (point : Fin params.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ params.extendedDirectLd)
   223	    (right : Option (PauliScalar params) → Op (setting.ExpandedLocalSpace second.side)) :
   224	    (∑ answer, stateQForm setting.psiHat
   225	      (setting.place first (((sublines.extendedMeasurement lines first.side line).postprocess
   226	        (fun polynomial => (directEvalOpt line point polynomial).map
   227	          (extendedDirectScalarEquiv params))).effect answer) *
   228	            setting.place second (right answer))) =
   229	      avgOver (sublines.conditionalLaw line) (fun sample =>

   265	/-- The actual extended-line versus extended-point overlap. Both families use
   266	the supplied witnesses and the source polynomial combination. -/
   267	def extendedPointOverlap {params : AdmissibleParams} {error pointError lineError : ℝ}
   268	    (setting : ProjectiveSetting params error) (points : CombinedPointsWitness setting pointError)
   269	    (lines : CombinedLinesWitness setting points lineError) (sublines : SubLineWitness params)
   270	    (first second : Placement)

   272	      (Fin params.extendedDirectLd.m → DirectScalarQ params.extendedDirectLd)) : ℝ :=

   377	/-- The ordered Z-then-X point overlap on the actual subline law. -/
   378	def orderedSublineOverlap {params : AdmissibleParams} {error pointError lineError : ℝ}

   383	    let point := directPointToPauli params (sample.1.base + parameter • sample.1.direction)

   388	              (evalOpt sample.2.2 (projZ point) pair.2) *

   392	/-- The first-route replacement by the ordered point product holds for any
   393	placement, in particular for the missing second-player orientation. Its only
   394	distributional input is the uniform joint point marginal, not a product law
   395	conditional on the projected lines. -/
   396	theorem SubLineWitness.paired_ordered_overlap_gap_le {params : AdmissibleParams}
   397	    {error pointError lineError : ℝ} {setting : ProjectiveSetting params error}
   398	    {points : CombinedPointsWitness setting pointError}
   399	    (sublines : SubLineWitness params) (lines : CombinedLinesWitness setting points lineError)
